# Agent Workspace

> A self-hosted control plane around the Claude Agent SDK: workspaces, people, agents, skills,
> tool servers, models and sandboxes managed in one place and exposed through one API, so the
> same agents can be driven from its own screens, a backend, a frontend, or a terminal. This
> file is the reading index for coding agents and language models working in this repository.

Generated by `pnpm docs:generate` (`scripts/docs/generate-llms-txt.mjs`) from the documents
it lists and from the docs site's navigation; `pnpm docs:check` fails when it is stale.
Regenerate it, do not edit it. Paths are relative to the repository root. A docs-site page
(`docs/sdk/site/<page>.mdx`) is served at `/<page>` when the site runs (`npx mint dev` in
`docs/sdk/site`). The site's reference pages and its OpenAPI document are generated from the
contracts, the SDK and the CLI source and are listed last, under Optional.

The order matters: the repository rules first, then what the product is and where it is going,
then the guides, then the resource-by-resource detail.

## Start here

- [Repository Instructions for Coding Agents](AGENTS.md): The operational checklist for coding agents: the working agreement, the required verification, the pull-request rules.
- [Claude Development Instructions](CLAUDE.md): Instructions for Claude Code in this repository: what to read first and the per-task procedure.
- [Engineering Guidelines](ENGINEERING_GUIDELINES.md): The rules for production code, tests and agent changes; a repository-wide gate is weakened only by an ADR.
- [Architecture](docs/architecture.md): System shape, what each application and package owns and must not own, the dependency direction and the trust boundaries — enforced by dependency-cruiser.
- [Testing strategy](docs/testing-strategy.md): Where a test goes, the CI gates that keep tests honest (no skips, coverage floors, ratchets) and how to run each lane locally.
- [Agent Workspace docs site](docs/sdk/site/README.md): How the docs site is previewed, checked and generated, and the Today / Target callout convention every page follows.

## Docs site: Start here

- [Overview](docs/sdk/site/index.mdx): The map of these docs: the seven chapters a developer goes through, from a first agent on a laptop to an agent in production on your own servers, and optionally on other platforms, and where each task lives.
- [What Agent Workspace is](docs/sdk/site/concepts/what-is-agent-workspace.mdx): The product in one page: a self-hosted control plane around the Claude Agent SDK — workspaces, people, agents, skills, connectors and runtimes managed in one place, and embeddable in your own product through one API.

## Docs site: 1 · Run your first agent

- [Chapter 1: Run your first agent](docs/sdk/site/path/first-agent.mdx): Have a customer-support agent answering on your laptop, in the browser and in the terminal, with one Node process and no Docker. About a minute from the first command.
- [Installation](docs/sdk/site/getting-started/installation.mdx): Before you begin: Node 24, an Anthropic API key, a non-elevated shell, about 600 MB of disk and one minute. Then, to add Agent Workspace to an app you already have: the SDK and the aw command line from npm.
- [Quickstart](docs/sdk/site/getting-started/quickstart.mdx): Your first agent in about a minute: set the key, npm create, npm run dev, then chat with it in the browser and the terminal, change it and watch it update, and run its evaluations. One Node process, no Docker.
- [Console tour](docs/sdk/site/getting-started/console-tour.mdx): Sign in to the web console of your local runtime and see each screen: the agent and its versions, runs, skills, files, connectors, models, runtimes and API keys, and which chapter uses each.
- [aw chat](docs/sdk/site/cli/chat.mdx): Talk to an agent from the terminal: the interactive loop, one-shot mode, and the SDK calls behind both.
- [Troubleshooting](docs/sdk/site/getting-started/troubleshooting.mdx): Fixes for the problems a first install can hit: a missing or rejected key, a busy port, an elevated Windows shell, Windows Node under WSL, the Docker sandbox, the widget on another origin, and the known issues of 0.6.9.

## Docs site: 2 · Build your agent

- [Chapter 2: Build your agent](docs/sdk/site/path/build.mdx): Give your agent its instructions, engine, model, skills, tools and credentials, all as files you commit.
- [Agents as code](docs/sdk/site/guides/agents-as-code.mdx): Keep agents and surfaces as TypeScript files, check them with aw check, save them as versions with aw push --yes, then promote and roll back.
- [Design an agent](docs/sdk/site/building/agents.mdx): Create an agent with least-privilege permissions, give it files, skills and connectors, pick its engine, and know what each setting controls at runtime.
- [Choose models and runtimes](docs/sdk/site/building/models-and-runtimes.mdx): Connect a model provider, pick the model for an agent or a single run, and choose where the agent's code runs.
- [Author a skill](docs/sdk/site/building/skills.mdx): Write a SKILL.md directory, import and update it, give it to an agent, and keep it in a project.
- [Tools from code](docs/sdk/site/guides/tools-from-code.mdx): Give an agent a function from your codebase with defineTool(), run by a tool host that aw dev starts, or an HTTP API with openapiTool() and secret(), where a write runs only for an approved call.
- [Tell a tool who is asking](docs/sdk/site/guides/caller-identity.mdx): Start a run with a subject, opt a connector in with identity, and check the signed x-aw-identity header in your own server with verifyIdentity().
- [Connect an MCP server](docs/sdk/site/building/mcp-servers.mdx): Register an MCP server as a connector, test it, store its credential safely and give it to an agent, and see how it reaches the model.
- [Build an agent in chat](docs/sdk/site/guides/build-an-agent-in-chat.mdx): Describe the agent you want and the Builder drafts it with you: what it asks before it saves, tries or runs evaluations, what the approval card shows, and what to do after a save.
- [Use the Builder tools from Claude Code](docs/sdk/site/guides/builder-tools-from-claude-code.mdx): Register a Builder client, connect Claude Code to your workspace with one claude mcp add command, and read the catalogue, the examples and the draft checks as yourself.
- [Secrets](docs/sdk/site/resources/secrets.mdx): Store credentials a workspace's agents and connections need, and rotate them without ever reading them back.
- [Use your own bucket](docs/sdk/site/guides/storage-connections.mdx): Connect an S3, Google Cloud Storage or Azure Blob bucket, or a local folder, give an agent a folder in it, run the agent and read what it wrote back.

## Docs site: 3 · Test and improve it

- [Chapter 3: Test and improve it](docs/sdk/site/path/test.mdx): See every run your agent makes, with its tool calls and cost, and keep an eval suite that catches a regression before you push.
- [Observability](docs/sdk/site/resources/observability.mdx): Recent run telemetry and the audit trail — an operator's glance, not the durable run store.
- [Evaluations](docs/sdk/site/guides/evaluations.mdx): Write test cases for an agent in its evals file, run them against the draft with aw eval, gate promotion on the score, and run them in CI.
- [Testing](docs/sdk/site/guides/testing.mdx): Test code that calls the SDK without a network: inject the recording fetch double from @indx-workspace/sdk/testing, answer with contract-valid fixtures, and simulate every failure and stream shape.

## Docs site: 4 · Put it in your product

- [Chapter 4: Put it in your product](docs/sdk/site/path/embed.mdx): Let your users talk to the agent inside your own site or app, or have your backend call it, without a workspace API key ever reaching a browser.
- [Which surface for which job](docs/sdk/site/building/overview.mdx): A decision table from what you want to build to the surface you use for it — the SDK, the API's resources, the platform's extension points — and the page that shows how.
- [Authentication](docs/sdk/site/getting-started/authentication.mdx): The SDK's credential kinds, where an API key comes from, and which routes an API key can never call.
- [Build a frontend](docs/sdk/site/building/frontend.mdx): Which credential a browser page can actually use, showing a surface's chat in React, rendering a live run, and listing sessions and runs for a UI.
- [Embed an agent in your product](docs/sdk/site/building/embedding.mdx): Put an Agent Workspace agent inside your own application: a one-tag widget or a React chat, a backend that starts runs and relays their stream, a chat panel, a canvas, agent switching, and a browser token in place of the relay.
- [Your own React](docs/sdk/site/building/react.mdx): Put the surface chat in your own React app: render the Chat component against the project running under aw dev, replace a part such as the composer, or draw everything yourself with useConversation.
- [Integrate a backend](docs/sdk/site/building/backend.mdx): Run agents from your own server or CI job: which role to mint an API key with, start-and-wait vs. streaming, polling instead of webhooks, stopping a run, and mapping SDK errors onto your own API.
- [Call the API without the SDK](docs/sdk/site/building/http-api.mdx): Call /api/** from Python, Go, a shell script or any HTTP stack: authenticate, read responses and errors, stream a run, move files, and generate a typed client from the OpenAPI document.
- [Streaming](docs/sdk/site/guides/streaming.mdx): Watch a run live: follow its events and print the agent's answer, survive dropped connections, resume from a saved cursor, parse a stream you already hold, and render tool calls and usage from the neutral agent.* events.
- [Get typed data back from a run](docs/sdk/site/guides/structured-output.mdx): Ask a run for a value of your own shape instead of parsing its text: pass a Zod schema from code or a JSON Schema file from the CLI, and read the result typed.

## Docs site: 5 · Ship it to your servers

- [Chapter 5: Ship it to your servers](docs/sdk/site/path/ship.mdx): Run your agent in production on your own VM, Google Cloud Run or Kubernetes, and move agents between workspaces without copying a secret.
- [Deploy](docs/sdk/site/guides/deploy.mdx): Name a production environment in agent-workspace.yaml and take it to a single VM, Google Cloud Run or Kubernetes with aw deploy production: it plans by default and applies with --yes.
- [Deploy on Vercel](docs/sdk/site/guides/deploy-vercel.mdx): Put the whole app on Vercel with agent-workspace deploy --target vercel, run sessions and code tools on E2B, push and promote an agent, call it through the API, hosted chat and the widget, and roll back.
- [Deploy on Cloudflare](docs/sdk/site/guides/deploy-cloudflare.mdx): Put the whole app on Cloudflare with agent-workspace deploy --target cloudflare, run sessions and code tools on E2B, push and promote an agent, call it through the API, hosted chat and the widget, and roll back.
- [Move an agent between workspaces](docs/sdk/site/building/moving-agents.mdx): Export an agent as a portable, name-keyed AgentDefinition and import it into another workspace or environment.
- [Self-host Agent Workspace](docs/sdk/site/building/self-hosting.mdx): Run the control plane yourself on a laptop, a single VM or Kubernetes: start it, finish the setup wizard, connect the SDK, and know which runtime drivers and security guarantees hold today.

## Docs site: 6 · Run it for your team

- [Chapter 6: Run it for your team](docs/sdk/site/path/operate.mdx): Give teammates roles and API keys, keep environments apart in separate workspaces, share agents, and know how the platform itself is extended.
- [Team](docs/sdk/site/resources/team.mdx): Members, users, invitations and API keys — the principals that can act in a workspace, spec §21's four roles.
- [Workspaces](docs/sdk/site/resources/workspaces.mdx): The tenant boundary itself: list, read, create and rename/archive/restore workspaces, and read or set the sharing policy.
- [Shares](docs/sdk/site/resources/shares.mdx): Publish a read-only snapshot of an agent, session, project or skill, and revoke it — plus what publish honestly does today.
- [Extend the platform](docs/sdk/site/building/extending-the-platform.mdx): The code-level extension points for a contributor working in the agent-workspace repository, and the gates that check each one.

## Docs site: 7 · Run it on other platforms

- [Chapter 7: Run it on other platforms](docs/sdk/site/path/platforms.mdx): Optional: take the agent you built to a hosted agent platform, switch the engine it runs on, or eject it to a standalone TypeScript project, with a report of what each move drops.
- [Export an agent to another platform](docs/sdk/site/platforms/overview.mdx): Compile your agent into the files of a hosted agent platform or a standalone project with aw platforms export, read the report of what maps and what is dropped, and import an agent back.
- [Claude Managed Agents](docs/sdk/site/platforms/claude-managed-agents.mdx): Export an agent to Claude Managed Agents as Markdown agent files, skills and an environment, learn which options it needs, and publish with Anthropic's ant tool.
- [Copilot Studio](docs/sdk/site/platforms/copilot-studio.mdx): Export an agent to Microsoft Copilot Studio as a cloned-agent folder with MCP actions and knowledge files, learn the options and limits, and pack it with the Power Platform CLI.
- [Microsoft 365 declarative agent](docs/sdk/site/platforms/m365-declarative-agent.mdx): Export an agent as a Microsoft 365 Copilot declarative agent app package with plugins for its MCP servers, learn what Microsoft 365 Copilot drops, and provision it with the Agents Toolkit.
- [Microsoft Foundry](docs/sdk/site/platforms/microsoft-foundry.mdx): Export an agent to Microsoft Foundry Agent Service as a prompt-agent definition per agent plus a project plan, learn the model deployment option, and publish with your own az login, plan first.
- [Gemini Enterprise](docs/sdk/site/platforms/gemini-enterprise.mdx): Register your agent in Gemini Enterprise over the A2A protocol: export an Agent Card and a registration request, keep the agent running on your deployment, and publish the registration with gcloud.
- [AWS AgentCore](docs/sdk/site/platforms/aws-agentcore.mdx): Export an agent as an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore harness project, learn the options and the model mapping it needs, and deploy it with the agentcore tool.
- [Eject to plain code](docs/sdk/site/platforms/eject.mdx): Generate a standalone TypeScript project for the Claude Agent SDK, Mastra or the OpenAI Agents SDK from your agent, run it with Node, and learn what it no longer has.
- [Switch the engine](docs/sdk/site/platforms/switch-engine.mdx): Change the agent loop an agent runs on, from the Claude Agent SDK to the OpenAI Agents SDK, pi or Mastra, and keep the platform; learn what changes per engine and which switches are refused.
- [Platform compatibility matrix](docs/sdk/site/platforms/matrix.mdx): What each agent platform and eject target carries natively, what it maps and what it drops, generated from the targets' own declarations.

## Docs site: Product tour

- [Your agent, your stack, on your own servers](docs/sdk/site/features/your-stack.mdx): Choose the engine, the model, the skills, the tools, the frontend and where it runs; see how each choice becomes a flag and a committed file, how a setting compiles into Claude Agent SDK options, and what does not work yet.
- [Agents are code. Here is the code.](docs/sdk/site/features/agents-skills-tools-as-code.mdx): One folder holds an agent, its skills, tools, surfaces and evals. What each file does, what the loader allows, how the same agent appears in the browser, and how to go from a tutorial to your own agent.
- [Five commands. The same agent all the way through.](docs/sdk/site/features/run-observe-evaluate.mdx): Scaffold and run an agent locally, talk to it with aw chat, score it with aw eval, save versions and promote them behind a score, deploy to a single VM or Cloud Run, and read every run as plain language, a trace, a record or an OpenTelemetry span.
- [Put the agent on a page: one tag, or React](docs/sdk/site/features/embed-in-your-product.mdx): Run an agent from your backend and stream what it does, keep the API key on the server, publish a surface as a one-tag widget or a React chat, allow the origins that may embed it, and share a snapshot of an agent, session, project or skill.
- [Built for the review your security team will do](docs/sdk/site/features/self-host-securely.mdx): Where Agent Workspace keeps your data, how model keys stay out of the agent's sandbox, what each runtime isolates, who can do what, what is audited, and what is not verified yet.

## Docs site: How it works

- [Design principles](docs/sdk/site/concepts/design-principles.mdx): Why Agent Workspace is shaped the way it is — the three values a developer should get from it, the eight principles that keep them true in the code, and what each one still costs today.
- [SDK architecture](docs/sdk/site/concepts/architecture.mdx): The three packages a consumer writes code against, the dependency direction between them, what each owns, and the trust boundary every response crosses.
- [The data plane](docs/sdk/site/concepts/data-plane.mdx): Where the platform keeps state, bytes, secrets and sandboxes — a contract the operator configures once per cloud and the developer never sees — with the cells that are verified today.
- [Run lifecycle](docs/sdk/site/concepts/run-lifecycle.mdx): How a run moves from queued to a terminal status, what usage and cost mean, sessions versus runs, and the event stream that reports it all.
- [Runtime neutrality](docs/sdk/site/concepts/runtime-neutrality.mdx): What every engine must honour or refuse by name, what stays engine-native, and the neutral AgentEvent view computed from relayed events.
- [Workspaces and principals](docs/sdk/site/concepts/workspaces-and-principals.mdx): The tenancy model — workspaces, principals, membership roles, and which credential to use for which job.
- [Ownership and sharing](docs/sdk/site/concepts/ownership-and-sharing.mdx): Who may create, change, assign and run each resource: the workspace as the boundary, ownership by principal, and the catalog → assignment → grant vocabulary — with the role table the server actually enforces
- [Public surface and stability](docs/sdk/site/concepts/public-surface.mdx): The four surfaces of Agent Workspace — what you consume, what you configure, what you may extend, and what is internal — and the compatibility promise each one carries.

## Docs site: SDK client in depth

- [Configuration](docs/sdk/site/getting-started/configuration.mdx): Point the client at your control plane, add headers, set a timeout, cancel a call, bring your own fetch, the environment variable convention this documentation uses, and the one URL that tells the server where files live.
- [Errors](docs/sdk/site/guides/errors.mdx): Every SDK call fails in one of four typed ways. Branch on the class and a stable code, and know at a glance which failures are worth retrying.
- [Timeouts and cancellation](docs/sdk/site/guides/timeouts-and-cancellation.mdx): timeoutMs covers response headers only; a caller's own AbortSignal is the only way to end a call or a stream at any later point.
- [Pagination](docs/sdk/site/guides/pagination.mdx): Walk every run, session or audit event with one cursor loop or a built-in listAll. Every other list method returns the whole collection in one call.
- [Retries and idempotency](docs/sdk/site/guides/retries-and-idempotency.mdx): The SDK retries nothing on its own except follow()'s reconnect. What is safe to retry yourself, and how an idempotency key keeps a retried runs.start from starting a run twice.

## Docs site: Resource guides

- [Agents](docs/sdk/site/resources/agents.mdx): Create, configure, and manage the reusable agent definitions that runs execute against.
- [Runs](docs/sdk/site/resources/runs.mdx): Start an agent against a prompt, stream what it does, and read its settled outcome.
- [Sessions](docs/sdk/site/resources/sessions.mdx): Read, rename, archive and restore platform sessions, and read the provider-native transcript stored under one.
- [Projects](docs/sdk/site/resources/projects.mdx): Group sessions under a name with shared defaults, archive and restore them, and attribute sessions to a project before their first run.
- [Files](docs/sdk/site/resources/files.mdx): Upload, list, move and delete the files and folders a workspace's agents can read and write.
- [Skills](docs/sdk/site/resources/skills.mdx): Import, read, edit and export the SKILL.md directories an agent can use.
- [Connectors](docs/sdk/site/resources/connectors.mdx): Register, test and rotate credentials for the MCP servers an agent can call.
- [Engines](docs/sdk/site/resources/engines.mdx): Discover which harnesses a deployment can run an agent on, and what each one can honour.
- [Models](docs/sdk/site/resources/models.mdx): Store model-provider credentials as connections, and discover the models each one offers.
- [Runtimes](docs/sdk/site/resources/runtimes.mdx): Define where an agent executes — the driver, its sizing, and its network and filesystem policy.
- [Triggers](docs/sdk/site/resources/triggers.mdx): Start a run of one agent from a webhook URL, without a person at the keyboard.

## Docs site: CLI

- [aw overview](docs/sdk/site/cli/overview.mdx): What the aw CLI does, how to install it, and the few commands that connect to a control plane, run an agent and drive a project.
- [aw dev in depth](docs/sdk/site/cli/dev.mdx): Everything aw dev prints and accepts: the ready screen line by line, its flags, the port rules, the model and runtime profile the first run uses, what npm create asks, aw init, and stopping it.
- [Configuration](docs/sdk/site/cli/configuration.mdx): Point aw at a control plane, switch between several with profiles, pass a key safely in scripts and CI, set a timeout, and send aw dev's model calls through your own gateway, with the exact precedence and every flag.
- [Output and exit codes](docs/sdk/site/cli/output-and-exit-codes.mdx): How aw renders a result for a person or a script, the stderr error format, and what each exit code means.
- [Storage connections](docs/sdk/site/cli/storage.mdx): Connect a bucket or folder, rotate its credential and list it from the terminal with aw storage.
- [aw vs. the SDK](docs/sdk/site/cli/cli-vs-sdk.mdx): When to reach for the CLI instead of the SDK, a command-to-method table, and what only the SDK can do.

## Docs site: Where it is going

- [Target architecture](docs/sdk/site/concepts/target-architecture.mdx): What Agent Workspace is meant to be for a developer once it is finished: the product thesis, the end-to-end developer experience, the package layout, the API, the extension model, and the invariants — with today's state noted where it differs.
- [Migration roadmap](docs/sdk/site/concepts/roadmap.mdx): Every gap between Agent Workspace as it exists today — the platform and its SDK — and the target architecture, in one place: what is true now, what the target is, and where the work is tracked.

## Docs site: Use cases

- [Enterprise use-case gallery](docs/sdk/site/tutorials/index.mdx): Ten agents Japanese enterprises ask for, each built end to end with the Agent Workspace SDK and kept as a benchmark: what the SDK does today, what takes your own code, and what is missing, every verdict backed by a test.
- [Build an agent on your own stack](docs/sdk/site/tutorials/your-stack.mdx): Pick the engine (Claude Agent SDK, Mastra, OpenAI Agents SDK or pi), the model, the skills, the tools, the frontend and the infrastructure, and turn the choice into one command, two committed files and a deployment you run yourself.
- [Use cases](docs/sdk/site/concepts/use-cases.mdx): Six concrete shapes Agent Workspace takes — an in-product copilot, a team workspace with roles, backend automation, a locked-down review agent, a support agent employees can ask, and an agent that runs on the cloud you already approved — each mapped to the surfaces and pages that build it.

## Docs site: Enterprise use-case gallery

- [1. Manual search agent](docs/sdk/site/tutorials/manual-search.mdx): An agent that searches thousands of pages of maintenance manuals, writes its own queries, and answers with a 〔document p.page §section〕 citation the backend checks against what it actually found. Built with defineAgent, a skill, the platform's search_files and a surface.
- [2. CAD drawing agent](docs/sdk/site/tutorials/cad-drafting.mdx): An agent that finds the past drawing closest to a new part, proposes a change set the designer approves, and drafts a DXF from it, changing only what the requirements change and marking it 未検図. Built with defineAgent, a skill that runs a Node script, the platform's search_files, a gated Write, a page surface and a backend that checks every dimension.
- [3. Quotation agent](docs/sdk/site/tutorials/quotation.mdx): An agent that drafts a sheet-metal quote from a customer's part spec: it reads similar past orders and the rate table from the ERP through openapiTool, prices the part with a cost-model script, and the backend refuses any draft whose numbers differ from that script. The agent books the quote in the ERP itself, and only for a call a person approved.
- [4. Ringi review agent](docs/sdk/site/tutorials/ringi-review.mdx): An agent that reviews each ringi (approval request) filed in your workflow system against the authority matrix, the ringi rules and past precedents, and writes a review sheet with a clause for every finding. It can comment but never approve or reject. Your backend starts it once per revision for the person who filed the ringi, narrowed to the departments' precedents they may read; the run answers in the sheet, your backend re-checks the approval route, and the agent posts the sheet as a comment once a person approves that call.
- [5. Customer inquiry agent](docs/sdk/site/tutorials/customer-inquiry.mdx): A chat agent on the company site that reads one customer's tickets, e-mails, call notes and orders through a read-only openapiTool the CRM answers for the caller's signed identity, searches the FAQ with the built-in search_files, answers in keigo, and hands identity checks, refunds and complaints to an operator. Built with defineAgent, defineSurface, a skill and a CRM API that scopes by identity and masks personal data.
- [6. Excel consolidation & analysis agent](docs/sdk/site/tutorials/excel-consolidation.mdx): An agent that finds each branch's sales workbook with search_files, reads five incompatible layouts, proposes a column mapping a person confirms, consolidates with a script that keeps every value's file!sheet!cell, and explains the month-over-month change. The backend refuses an explanation that quotes a number the script did not compute.
- [7. Contract review agent](docs/sdk/site/tutorials/contract-review.mdx): An agent that reads a counterparty's Word draft clause by clause, applies the legal team's playbook through a deterministic detector script, and returns a risk table with playbook citations and redline proposals. Legal approves the redline before the Word file is made, and the backend refuses a review whose table leaves out a must-flag finding.
- [8. Meeting minutes & action-item agent](docs/sdk/site/tutorials/meeting-minutes.mdx): An agent that turns a Teams or Zoom transcript into formal 議事録 in the house format, resolves 来週金曜 and 3営業日後 to real dates, and registers action items in the task tracker only after a person approves them, using one run and one approval per item, a date script, an approved `openapiTool` write, and your own read-only tracker MCP server.
- [9. Skill-transfer & maintenance troubleshooting agent](docs/sdk/site/tutorials/maintenance-troubleshooting.mdx): A shop-floor agent that starts with lockout, then guides a junior technician through a fault one cited step at a time from past trouble records, equipment manuals and retiring experts' notes found with the built-in file search, narrowed to the signed-in technician's production lines, logs the fix in the maintenance system once the technician approves the call, and hands unsolved cases to the expert. The backend checks every turn.
- [10. Quality defect and past-trouble analysis agent](docs/sdk/site/tutorials/quality-defect.mdx): An agent that takes a new defect, finds similar past troubles (過去トラ), quotes 4M counts the database computed, and drafts a なぜなぜ chain and an 8D report for design review, with a backend that checks every Q-number, every count and the recurrence flag. Confidential: a policy ceiling keeps it offline.
